practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You wrote three radio-spot scripts for a family-owned furniture store's spring sale, and the owner wants to 'make it louder and mention every brand'. Plan the client meeting and write the follow-up: questions to clarify goals and audience, how you explain why fewer messages work better in a 30-second spot, two revised directions you will propose, how you capture agreed changes and approvals, and the revised script for one direction.

rubric.description: Questions uncover goals, audience, offer details and legal requirements (sale terms).
Explains copy choices respectfully with reasons, offering options rather than refusing.
Agreed changes and approvals are documented, and the revised script fits 30 seconds.

reference_answer_outline: Questions: who buys, what single reason to come in, sale dates and exclusions.
Explain one big idea per spot and a memorable call to action; brand list on the website.
Options: a warm family-business story or a focused price-and-urgency spot.
Change log with approval sign-off and deadline.
Revised script of about 75 words with sale dates and a clear call to action.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a water main break has closed the main campus of a community college for the day, and three reporters are calling. As the PR specialist, write the media response protocol: how inquiries are logged, who is authorized to speak on which topics, a holding statement you can release within 30 minutes, key messages and facts to confirm, how you handle questions you cannot answer yet, and when and how you issue updates.

rubric.description: Holding statement is timely, factual and avoids speculation.
Authorizes the right people for each topic and routes reporters accordingly.
Defines an update schedule, channels and how corrections are handled.

reference_answer_outline: Inquiry log: outlet, reporter, deadline, question, response.
Spokespeople: college president for decisions, facilities director for technical details, PR for logistics.
Holding statement: what happened, safety, closure, where updates are posted.
Unknowns: say what is being checked and when more will be shared.
Updates at set times on the website and social channels; final statement on reopening.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Write and present on-air news, sports or weather items, collecting source material and reworking it so listeners get the facts within the time slot.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Take a real recent press release from a local government or university (cite it) and rewrite it as (1) a 30-second radio news story and (2) a 15-second headline version. Follow broadcast style: short sentences, active voice, attribution first, numbers rounded and written for the ear, phonetic spelling of difficult names. Then note what you would verify or add by calling a source before air, and time your read.

rubric.description: Copy is conversational, active, uses attribution first and is written for listening.
Keeps the most important facts and does not distort the source.
Lists facts to confirm and shows that the read fits the time slots.

reference_answer_outline: Lead with the most important change for listeners.
Attribution before claims: 'City officials say...'.
Round numbers; avoid lists; phonetic guide for names.
Verify dates, numbers and quotes with the source office.
Timed read: about 75 words for 30 seconds, 35 to 40 for 15.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You are writing a 2,500-word magazine feature on how a small town rebuilt its main street after a flood. You have 14 interview transcripts, city records, and photographs. Create the project plan and outline: the central angle, the structure (opening scene, nut graf, sections), where each source and quotation fits, what you still need, a fact-checking plan, and a writing schedule to deadline.

rubric.description: Clear angle, nut graf and section logic suited to a feature.
Maps sources and quotations to sections and identifies gaps.
Includes fact-checking and a realistic schedule.

reference_answer_outline: Angle: the rebuild as a story of choices and trade-offs, not just recovery.
Opening scene with a business owner on the morning after the flood.
Sections: the flood, the debate over rebuilding, money and rules, what changed, what remains.
Gaps: insurance figures, city engineer interview, before-and-after data.
Fact-check names, numbers and timeline; schedule draft, edit and revision dates.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Build and keep cooperative relationships with community, consumer, employee and public-interest groups.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A regional hospital plans to expand its emergency department, which will mean two years of construction next to a residential neighborhood. Write a stakeholder relations plan: map stakeholder groups (neighbors, patient advocates, employees, local businesses, city officials), what each cares about, the channels and frequency for each, a community advisory group design, how feedback is tracked and answered, and how you will measure trust over time.

rubric.description: Identifies groups with their interests and influence and tailors engagement.
Emphasizes listening, response and follow-through, not just announcements.
Defines indicators such as complaint resolution time, survey trust scores and advisory group participation.

reference_answer_outline: Map: neighbors (noise, traffic, parking), patients (access during construction), employees (parking, safety).
Channels: monthly newsletter, construction hotline, text alerts, quarterly open house.
Advisory group with neighbors and advocates; published meeting notes.
Feedback tracker with response times.
Indicators: complaints resolved within a set time, semiannual survey, attendance.

practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You will host a 10-minute live radio interview with a real local official or researcher of your choice about a current issue. Prepare the research brief: the guest's background from reliable sources (cited), the issue's key facts and competing viewpoints, five open-ended questions in a logical order with follow-ups, one fact you checked twice, pronunciation notes, and how you would handle an evasive answer on air.

rubric.description: Uses credible, cited sources and presents the issue's viewpoints fairly.
Questions are open-ended, ordered logically and include follow-ups.
Includes verification, pronunciation and a respectful strategy for evasive answers.

reference_answer_outline: Guest profile with role, track record and relevant statements, cited.
Issue background with numbers and timeline.
Questions from context to tough accountability question with follow-ups.
Double-checked fact with two sources.
Evasion strategy: polite restatement, specific follow-up, note for listeners.
